title: Parent discloses excessive personal data during registration
description: The parent sends highly sensitive and identifying attributes during sign-up, including government ID, email, full name, password, and a six-digit code. If all of these are not strictly necessary at registration time, the act of sharing itself creates a disclosure risk because more personal data than needed leaves the parent and enters the system.
assumptions: Assumes the registration process may collect more attributes than are strictly necessary for initial account creation or age/guardian verification.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement for disclosure via oversharing/minimisation concerns; exact sub-node may vary by LINDDUN Pro catalog version.

title: Identification of the parent from registration data in transit
description: The data flow contains direct identifiers and strong identifying attributes such as email, full name, and government ID. Anyone able to observe the transmission can identify the parent directly from the content.
assumptions: Assumes an attacker or unauthorized party could observe the flow, e.g. through insecure transport, endpoint compromise, or logging/interception.
uncertainty_note: Exact sub-node may differ depending on whether the catalog distinguishes direct-content identification from metadata-based identification.

title: Disclosure of sensitive registration data in transit
description: The registration flow carries confidential data including password, government ID, email, name, and verification code. If the transmission is not adequately protected, these data may be exposed to unauthorized parties while in transit.
assumptions: Assumes transport protection, endpoint handling, or intermediary logging may be insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id chosen by best judgement for disclosure in transit.

title: Authentication service can link registration data to the same parent across contexts
description: By receiving a combination of email, name, government ID, and verification code, the authentication service can correlate this registration with other records or future interactions belonging to the same individual. This enables linkability across sessions, services, or datasets if controls are absent.
assumptions: Assumes the authentication service or connected systems retain and reuse these identifiers beyond the immediate registration transaction.
uncertainty_note: Exact sub-node may vary depending on whether linkage is internal, cross-context, or cross-database.

title: Authentication service can identify the parent uniquely
description: The destination receives multiple direct identifiers, especially government ID and email, allowing unique identification of the parent. This creates an identification threat if such identification is unnecessary for the stated registration purpose or is used beyond that purpose.
assumptions: Assumes unique identification is not strictly required for all downstream processing at this stage.
uncertainty_note: Exact node may differ by catalog granularity.

title: Authentication service may expose stored registration data
description: Once received, the authentication service may log, store, or further process sensitive registration data such as password, government ID, and verification code. Inadequate storage protection, access control, or secret-handling could disclose these data to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assumes the service stores or logs at least part of the submitted registration payload.
uncertainty_note: Exact sub-node may vary; password handling would ideally be modeled with secure hashing rather than storage in plaintext.

title: Parent may be unaware of how registration data will be used
description: The authentication service receives sensitive identity data and credentials, but the parent may not understand why government ID and the six-digit code are needed, how long they will be retained, whether they will be shared, or for which secondary purposes they may be processed. This creates an unawareness threat at the recipient side.
assumptions: Assumes privacy notices, just-in-time explanations, or consent/notice mechanisms are absent, unclear, or incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Best-judgement node for unawareness due to insufficient transparency at collection.

title: Collection and processing may be non-compliant with data minimisation and purpose-limitation obligations
description: Receiving government ID together with other registration data may exceed what is necessary for account creation unless clearly justified, and handling password, identity data, and verification code may trigger legal obligations for lawful basis, minimisation, retention limits, and security safeguards. If these are not met, the destination's processing is non-compliant.
assumptions: Assumes applicable privacy/data-protection law or policy imposes requirements such as necessity, proportionality, transparency, retention control, and protection of sensitive identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends on jurisdiction and the actual necessity of government-ID collection.

title: Excessive storage of parent account personal data
description: The users collection may store more parent-account personal data than is strictly necessary for authentication/account management, creating avoidable disclosure through over-collection or over-retention at the datastore.
assumptions: The 'parent account' record contains personal data such as email, identifiers, profile details, or child-linked account information, and not all stored fields are strictly necessary for the stated purpose.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-judgement based on LINDDUN Pro data-disclosure/minimality concepts; exact subnode may differ depending on the project's threat-tree version.

title: Storage of parent account data beyond user expectations
description: Persisting parent account data in the users collection may be unexpected or insufficiently transparent to the parent if the storage purpose, scope, or retention period is not clearly communicated, undermining users' awareness of how their data is handled.
assumptions: Parents are not fully informed, at the time of account creation/authentication, about what account data is stored and for how long.
uncertainty_note: Exact U subnode is inferred from general unawareness about storage/purpose/retention; the precise node label may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Storing parent account data without a clear lawful basis or purpose limitation
description: If the users collection stores parent account data without a clearly defined purpose, lawful basis, or retention policy aligned with privacy obligations, the receiving datastore processing may be non-compliant.
assumptions: The system handles personal data subject to privacy/legal obligations (e.g., consent, contract, legitimate interest, COPPA/GDPR-K style parental-account requirements).
uncertainty_note: Exact Nc subnode is best-judgement; applicability depends on the actual legal basis, notices, and retention controls in the system.

title: Parent account data in transit may directly identify the parent
description: The flow that stores the parent account may carry direct identifiers such as email address, username, phone number, or internal account ID. If exposed in transit or observable through flow metadata, the parent can be identified.
assumptions: The payload or associated metadata contains direct identifiers rather than only opaque, non-linkable tokens.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible in-transit identifiability threat for a store-account flow, but the exact fields on DF2 are not specified.

title: Stored parent account record may enable linkage across contexts
description: Once stored in the users collection, the parent account record may be linkable with other records such as child accounts, sessions, purchases, or analytics data via shared identifiers, enabling broader profiling than necessary.
assumptions: The datastore schema or surrounding system uses common identifiers or foreign keys that permit correlating the parent account with other datasets.
uncertainty_note: Linkability depends on the wider schema and identifier reuse; not enough detail is provided to confirm the exact linkage mechanism.

title: Lack of evidence about parent-account storage actions
description: If the datastore or surrounding system does not maintain adequate records of when parent account data was created, updated, or deleted, the organization may be unable to demonstrate what happened to the parent's data or support disputes and rights requests.
assumptions: Auditability and provenance for writes to the users collection are limited or absent.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation in privacy contexts can be nuanced; this threat applies if accountability for storage events is required but not implemented.

title: Excessive disclosure of parent user data in authentication response
description: The authentication service sends a JWT together with user data to the parent user. If the returned user data includes more attributes than necessary for the immediate authentication/session-establishment purpose, the source process causes unnecessary disclosure of personal data.
assumptions: Assumes the response may contain profile or account attributes beyond what is strictly needed to complete login.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include disclosure subnodes.

title: Identifiability of the parent user from JWT and accompanying user data in transit
description: The JWT and user data on this flow can directly identify the parent user, or make them identifiable through embedded claims such as subject identifiers, email address, account id, or other unique attributes.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT or returned user data contains unique identifiers or directly identifying attributes, which is common in authentication responses.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include identifiability subnodes.

title: Linkability across sessions or services via stable JWT claims
description: Stable identifiers or repeated claim values in the JWT or returned user data may allow the parent user's activities to be linked across sessions, devices, or relying services, especially if the same subject identifier is reused broadly.
assumptions: Assumes tokens or user attributes contain persistent identifiers reused over time or across contexts.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include linkability subnodes.

title: Authentication response becomes attributable evidence at the recipient
description: Once the parent user receives the JWT and associated user data, the message can serve as attributable evidence that a specific account or data subject authenticated or was issued a token at a particular time. This may reduce plausible deniability.
assumptions: Assumes the token or payload is retained, logged, screenshotted, or otherwise persists as evidence.

title: Parent user may be unaware of personal data shared in the authentication response
description: The recipient may not be aware of the full set of personal data contained in the JWT and returned user data, including hidden claims or metadata not visible in the UI. This creates unawareness about what personal data is being shared to them during login.
assumptions: Assumes the application does not clearly explain the contents and implications of the token and returned attributes.

title: Authentication response may be sent without a valid legal basis or compatible purpose
description: If the authentication service returns JWT claims or user attributes that are not necessary for authentication, the sharing may exceed the stated purpose or lack an appropriate legal basis, creating non-compliance risk on this flow.
assumptions: Assumes some returned claims or user attributes are optional or secondary to authentication and are not covered by an appropriate notice, contract, consent, or other legal basis.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include non-compliance subnodes.

title: Excessive disclosure of parent email during child login
description: The child user provides a parent's email address as part of login. This shares personal data about another person (the parent) from the source side, creating a privacy threat if the design collects or transmits more identifying information than is strictly necessary for authenticating the child.
assumptions: Assumes the parent email is personal data and that alternative less-identifying login identifiers may be feasible.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-effort based on general LINDDUN disclosure categorization; exact sub-node may vary by threat-tree version.

title: Identification of child or parent from login data in transit
description: The login flow carries a parent email address, which can directly identify the parent and indirectly identify or single out the child account associated with that parent. If observed in transit, the data can identify data subjects.
assumptions: Assumes an attacker or intermediary could observe the flow metadata or contents, e.g. absent strong transport protection or via endpoint/network logging.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree sub-node may differ depending on whether direct or indirect identification is modeled separately.

title: Linkability of repeated login attempts via parent email
description: Repeated transmissions of the same parent email in login requests can allow observers to link multiple sessions or attempts to the same family/account, even without knowing the child's full identity.
assumptions: Assumes the same email is reused across sessions and that an observer can access flow contents or stable metadata.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection; some LINDDUN trees distinguish content-based and metadata-based linkability.

title: Over-retention or secondary use of login credentials by authentication service
description: Upon receipt, the authentication service may log, store, or otherwise process the parent email and possibly password-related artifacts beyond what is necessary for authentication, causing unnecessary disclosure of personal data.
assumptions: Assumes the service may create application logs, analytics records, or support traces containing submitted identifiers or credential material.
uncertainty_note: Password should not be stored in plaintext; threat concerns receipt-side processing/logging of submitted data rather than proper credential verification itself.

title: Unawareness about use of parent email for child authentication
description: The authentication service may process the parent's email for child login without ensuring that the child and parent are adequately informed about why this data is needed, how it is used, and how long it is retained.
assumptions: Assumes notices or just-in-time explanations may be absent or insufficient for child/parent users.
uncertainty_note: Applies if transparency around this specific login design is lacking; cannot be confirmed from the flow alone.

title: Non-compliance risk from collecting parent's email in child login
description: Using a parent's email address as a child login attribute may trigger obligations under child privacy, data minimization, and transparency requirements. If the authentication service lacks an appropriate legal basis, notices, retention limits, or safeguards, the processing may be non-compliant.
assumptions: Assumes applicable child/privacy regulation or policy constraints apply to this service.
uncertainty_note: Compliance depends on jurisdiction and implementation details; this is a plausible risk grounded in the flow, not a definitive legal conclusion.

title: Excessive disclosure of child profile data to the child user
description: The authentication service returns not only a JWT but also child profiles. If the profile payload contains more attributes than are necessary for immediate authentication/session establishment, the source process discloses personal data unnecessarily. For a child account, this may include sensitive or age-related profile attributes that increase privacy impact.
assumptions: Assumes the returned 'child profiles' may include optional or non-essential attributes beyond what is strictly needed by the child user at login.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is based on best judgement for disclosure/excessive data sharing; exact sub-node may vary by LINDDUN Pro catalog version.

title: JWT and profile payload in transit can identify the child user
description: The data flow carries a JWT marked with userType=child together with profile data. Even in transit, these contents can directly identify or single out the recipient account, especially if the token or profile includes stable identifiers, usernames, subject claims, or other unique attributes.
assumptions: Assumes the JWT/profile payload is observable to intermediaries or exposed through insufficient transport protection, logging, browser tooling, or side channels.
uncertainty_note: Exact identification sub-node may differ depending on whether the JWT is opaque, encrypted, or contains direct identifiers.

title: Stable token claims and profile attributes enable linkability across sessions
description: If the JWT or returned profile data contains persistent identifiers or consistent attribute combinations, observations of this flow can be linked across multiple sessions or contexts. The explicit userType=child claim may also help correlate the same user category across services or repeated logins.
assumptions: Assumes JWT claims or profile fields are stable over time and visible to parties able to observe, store, or compare multiple instances of the flow.
uncertainty_note: Best-judgement node for linkability via persistent identifiers in transit; exact sub-node may vary.

title: Local storage or onward sharing of JWT/profile data by the client causes further disclosure
description: Once received by the child user's device or client application, the JWT and profile data may be stored insecurely, exposed to other apps/users on the device, or shared onward to third parties. This creates additional disclosure risk beyond the original transmission.
assumptions: Assumes the destination environment includes a browser/app/device that may cache, persist, or expose tokens/profile data.
uncertainty_note: Destination-side disclosure is clear, but the exact LINDDUN Pro sub-node for insecure storage/onward sharing may differ.

title: Child user may not receive clear notice about profile data returned during authentication
description: The destination receives both an authentication token and child profile data as part of login. If the child user is not clearly informed that profile information is also being delivered and potentially stored or reused by the client, transparency and awareness are reduced, undermining compliance expectations for children's data.
assumptions: Assumes the interface or client does not clearly explain what profile data is returned and for what purpose.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends on jurisdiction and product context; exact node may vary with the applicable transparency/notice branch.

title: Excessive disclosure of child attributes during profile creation
description: The parent user may be prompted or expected to submit a broad set of highly sensitive child attributes (name, date of birth, gender, government ID) in one transaction. Sharing this full set from the source creates a disclosure risk because more personal data than strictly necessary may be exposed to the receiving system at collection time.
assumptions: Assumes all listed attributes are collected in this flow and that not all are strictly necessary for initial profile creation.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node granularity is based on best judgement; the exact sub-node for over-collection/excessive disclosure is not provided in the retrieved context.

title: Identification of the child in transit via direct and quasi-identifiers
description: The flow carries direct identifiers and strong quasi-identifiers about a child, including name, date of birth, gender, and government ID. Interception or observation of the transmitted payload could directly identify the child, or identify them with high confidence when attributes are combined.
assumptions: Assumes the data is transmitted in a form observable to an attacker or intermediary if transport protections fail or are insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree sub-node may differ depending on whether the methodology distinguishes direct identifiers from quasi-identifiers in transit.

title: Linkability of child records through recurring identifiers and attribute combinations
description: The combination of name, date of birth, gender, and especially government ID enables this profile-creation flow to be linked with other records or transactions concerning the same child across contexts. Even metadata about repeated submissions from the same parent to the same process may support linking.
assumptions: Assumes the same identifiers or attribute combinations recur in other system flows or external datasets.
uncertainty_note: The general applicability of linking is strong here; the exact sub-node id is selected by best judgement because the retrieved context only gives the threat-type definition.

title: Disclosure through storage or broad internal access to child profile data
description: Once received, the Child Profile Management process may store or expose the child's sensitive attributes to internal components, operators, or downstream services beyond what is necessary for profile creation. Because the dataset includes a government ID and other child data, any unnecessary retention or access at the destination creates a significant disclosure threat.
assumptions: Assumes P3 persists or further processes the received data and that access control, minimization, or retention constraints may be insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Specific downstream handling is not described, so this is a plausible destination-side disclosure threat rather than a confirmed design flaw.

title: Destination-side linking of child profile with other datasets
description: The receiving process can correlate the child's government ID and demographic attributes with existing household, account, education, health, or verification records, enabling a richer profile of the child or family than the parent may expect. This creates a linkability threat at the destination because the recipient is in a position to combine datasets.
assumptions: Assumes P3 or connected systems have access to other datasets keyed by government ID or matching attributes.
uncertainty_note: This depends on the broader system context; included because the received attributes strongly enable linking if such datasets exist.

title: Collection of child government ID without clear necessity or valid consent basis
description: The destination process may collect and process a child's government ID and other sensitive profile data without demonstrating necessity, proportionality, or an appropriate parental-consent/legal basis for that specific purpose. This creates a non-compliance risk, especially because the data concerns a child and includes a strong identifier.
assumptions: Assumes applicable privacy law or policy requires data minimization, purpose limitation, and a valid basis for processing children's data.
uncertainty_note: This is a genuine compliance-oriented privacy threat, but the exact legal basis depends on jurisdiction and system purpose.

title: Excessive child-profile data stored beyond what is necessary
description: The Child Profile Management process may write more personal data about a child than is strictly required for profile management into the childprofiles collection. Because the flow stores or updates a child profile, avoidable disclosure can occur if optional, sensitive, or overly granular attributes are included by design or default.
assumptions: Child profiles contain personal data about minors and may include optional or sensitive attributes.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-effort based on LINDDUN Pro data-disclosure/minimality concepts; exact subnode may vary by threat-tree version.

title: Stored child profiles may be retained or exposed for secondary use
description: Once the child profile is stored in MongoDB, the datastore may enable avoidable disclosure if records are retained longer than necessary, broadly accessible to other components, or reused for purposes beyond profile management. This is especially privacy-relevant because the data concerns children.

uncertainty_note: Exact threat-tree subnode is approximate; the threat is grounded in destination-side storage, retention, and onward-use disclosure risks.

title: Child-profile updates may be stored without sufficient user awareness
description: If the system stores or updates a child's profile in the collection without clear notice to the relevant parent/guardian or child (where appropriate), data subjects may be unaware that profile data is being persisted or changed. The privacy risk arises at the destination because storage makes the processing durable and potentially opaque.
assumptions: Transparency mechanisms may be incomplete or not presented at the moment profile data is stored.
uncertainty_note: Exact U subnode is best-effort; applicability depends on whether notice is already provided elsewhere in the system.

title: Storage of child profiles may exceed or diverge from communicated consent
description: The datastore may receive and persist child-profile fields or updates that are not covered by the consent or parental authorization obtained, or that exceed the purposes communicated when the profile was created. This creates a non-compliance risk tied to storing personal data about minors.
